name: Revert a Bad Deploy
problem: You merged a pull request into `main` and deployed it, but it contains a critical bug that broke production. You need to undo it immediately without disrupting the team's history.

steps.title: Find the bad commit
steps.description: Look at the log to find the hash of the merge commit that introduced the bug.
steps.code:
git log --oneline

# Example output:
# a1b2c3d Merge pull request #42 from feature/broken
# e4f5g6h Fix typo in header

steps.title: Revert the merge commit
steps.description: Since it's a merge commit, you must use `-m 1` to tell Git to keep the main line of history and reject the branch that was merged.
steps.code:
git revert -m 1 a1b2c3d

# Git opens an editor with 'Revert "Merge pull request #42"'
# Save and close.

steps.title: Push the fix
steps.description: Push the revert commit to production immediately.

steps.title: Fix the actual bug (Later)
steps.description: When you're ready to fix the bug, you'll need to revert the revert (otherwise Git won't let you merge the branch again), then apply the fix.
steps.code:
git checkout -b feature/fix-broken

# Revert the revert commit:
git revert <hash-of-the-revert-commit>

# Now the broken code is back on your branch.
# Fix the bug, commit, and open a new PR.
